title: A joint runoff and recession test did not resolve a new leakage change after 1997 in 78 south-east Australian catchments
abstract: We test whether annual runoff retention and dry-weather recession jointly support a simple new loss process in south-east Australia. For a single store with an unchanged increasing storage-to-flow relation, proportional non-stream loss, equal effective input and no net storage trend, runoff retention times the recession multiplier must equal one. We join statistics from two published SCI studies. In 175 catchments in 2010-2021 the geometric product was 0.824, with a conditional 95% spatial interval of 0.738-0.902. Model and rain-product checks retained a gap. But a mismatch was also present in 1981-1996. On 78 common catchments, the post-period minus placebo result was -0.045 log units, with limits of -0.134 to +0.074. This did not resolve a new mismatch after 1997. An exact reservoir example shows that less effective input and a changed storage-to-flow coefficient can produce the same full flow record. The diagnostic narrows what the signatures can establish; it does not identify the regional physical cause or reject leakage in general. The test conditions on published fits, uses a limited placebo cohort and does not measure recharge. Code, compatible fit statistics, all uncertainty samples, proofs, figures, provenance and an arithmetic and water-balance audit are included.

display.caption: The joint restriction fails in the raw test. The paired change from the earlier-period test includes zero.
